title: Recursion and the call stack
summary: Every call gets its own frame on a stack. Watch the frames pile up and come off in reverse.

checkpoints.text: We'll print this list backwards without a loop and without changing a single pointer.
Four calls are waiting at once: one for each node, plus this one for NULL. Look at the stack panel: every frame has its own `node`. Calls are pushed on top of each other, like a stack of plates.
The NULL call returned, and its frame came off the top. We are back in the frame for node 3, so 3 prints first.
The frame for node 1 was the first call made and it finishes last. Last in, first out: the call stack is a stack.
3 2 1. Recursion that never reaches its base case keeps pushing frames until memory runs out: a stack overflow. HeapHop stops at 64 waiting calls.
